title: Machine cost, depreciation, and impairment — Oriole Co.
instructions: Oriole Co. acquired a machine on January 1, Year 1. It uses straight-line depreciation with a 5-year life and an **$11,000** salvage value. Determine the cost, then account for a Year 3 impairment.

exhibits.title: Costs related to the machine
exhibits.content:
| Item | Amount |
|---|---:|
| Invoice price (terms 2/10, n/30; paid within discount period) | 200,000 |
| Freight to Oriole's plant | 4,000 |
| Installation and testing | 10,000 |
| Insurance while in transit | 1,000 |
| Repair of damage caused by Oriole's crew during installation | 3,000 |
| One-year maintenance contract | 2,000 |

exhibits.title: December 31, Year 3 impairment review
exhibits.content:
Because of a drop in demand, Oriole tested the machine for recoverability:
- Undiscounted future net cash flows: **$85,000**
- Fair value: **$70,000**
- Remaining useful life: **2 years**; revised salvage value **$10,000**

rows.label: Invoice price, net of the cash discount
rows.explanation: Cost is the cash-equivalent price, net of the discount taken.

rows.label: Freight
rows.explanation: Necessary to get the asset to its location.

rows.label: Installation and testing
rows.explanation: Necessary to make the asset ready for use.

rows.label: Insurance in transit
rows.explanation: Part of getting the asset to its location.

rows.label: Repair of installation damage
rows.explanation: An avoidable cost that adds no service potential.

rows.label: Maintenance contract
rows.explanation: It benefits future operating periods, not acquisition (prepaid, then expensed).

rows.label: Carrying amount, Dec 31 Year 3, before impairment
